about: timetable's domain mutants; each is judged by the domain package's laws (ergo test examples/timetable/timetable), run by the examples suite, not by a compiler test.

mutants.name: T6 a skipped wall time leaves before the gap
mutants.rule: LeavesOnItsDay: a wall time the clock skips leaves at the first instant after the gap.

mutants.name: T6 a wall time shown twice leaves the second time
mutants.rule: LeavesOnItsDay: a wall time shown twice leaves the first time.

mutants.name: T6 departures miss the trains of two days before
mutants.rule: EveryCallIsListed: a stop's departures hold each call the stop's clock shows that day, of a train that left up to two days before.

mutants.name: T6 departures out of time order
mutants.rule: DeparturesAreOnTheDay: a stop's departures are in time order.

mutants.name: T6 a delay on the way moves nothing
mutants.from: Next: Running{Next: r.Next, Due: later(r.Due, d.By)}
mutants.rule: DelayMovesTheRest: a delay moves every instant still to come.

mutants.name: T6 a running train is cancelled
mutants.to:
case (Running, Cancel as x):
		Emit[Leg, Notice]{Next: Cancelled{Reason: x.Reason}, Output: Withdrawn{Reason: x.Reason}}
mutants.rule: CancelOnlyBeforeLeaving and NeverGoesBack: a train is cancelled only before it leaves.

mutants.name: T6 the picker shows a week too many
mutants.rule: WeeksFollowOneAnother: the picker shows the weeks asked for.
